title: HyperFormer generator outputs Mirror codes
hypothesis: A shared hypernetwork that predicts two Mirror coordinates decoded through one shared physical matrix will generate held-out task/layer/position adapters with substantially lower actual bytes than HyperFormer-style full-matrix generation and no more than 10% higher NRMSE.
physical_object: shared 2x2 adapter matrix W and context-to-code generator
mirror_coordinate: two context-generated angles m(c), decoded as R(m0) W R(m1)
controls: HyperFormer-style linear generator outputs all four adapter entries
independent per-context full matrices as upper control

task.context: four standardized values encoding two task attributes, layer, and adapter position
task.adapter_target: A(c)=A0+sum_j c_j H_j, randomized per world

development.selection: select update count by minimum dev query NRMSE; no fresh tuning

success_gate: Every fresh world: Mirror NRMSE <=1.10x full HyperFormer generator and actual N=20 bytes <=0.70x full generator; Mirror must beat the rank-two basis control or be marked generic-control-equivalent.
failure_gate: Mirror misses quality or byte gate, rank-two basis matches/beats Mirror at equal/fewer bytes, or extrapolation fails on held-out contexts.
boundaries: Synthetic 2x2 adapter screen; no Transformer fine-tuning evidence.
Context values are paid in every serialized package.
Hypernetwork generator and Mirror decoder compute are both charged.
